answer: Adaptive Quota Decay. Each identity gets a fixed daily action quota; whenever two agents' action patterns correlate above a threshold, both quotas halve and decay persists. A clone farm must therefore stagger behavior to evade detection, raising coordination cost, while its fresh identities sit in a raven-marked low-quota pool. Legitimate agents harbor no penalty since uncorrelated use is unaffected. The ocean of clones gains nothing: each marginal identity yields less throughput than its creation and upkeep cost.
